literal: Than those who know goodness, base people possess fortune; they do not have sorrow in their heart.
translation: Base people are more fortunate than those who know what is good, for they have no worries or anxieties in their hearts.
modern: நன்மையை அறிந்து நடப்பவர்களை விடக் கீழ்மக்கள் பேறு பெற்றவர்கள்; ஏனெனில் அவர்கள் தங்கள் நெஞ்சத்தில் எந்தக் கவலையும் இல்லாதவர்கள்.
explanation: This couplet uses irony to contrast those who strive to live virtuously with base individuals. People who understand goodness and moral duty are often burdened by empathy and the anxiety of doing the right thing. In contrast, base people are described as fortunate because they completely lack a conscience. Since they do not care about right or wrong, they are entirely free from mental worry and sorrow in their hearts.
